questions.prompt: A point at (1,0) is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the origin. What is its y-coordinate?

feedback.hint: Apply the 2D rotation matrix to (1,0).
feedback.solution: The rotated point is (0,1), so y=1.

questions.prompt: A planar arm has two 0.5 m links and both joints at 0°. What is the end-effector x-position in meters?

feedback.hint: At 0° both links extend along +x, so add their lengths.

questions.prompt: Why does feedback remain necessary after a collision-free path is planned?
options: The plan cannot account for every disturbance, calibration error, or state-estimation error
Feedback makes geometry unnecessary
A path plan determines actual forces exactly
It is needed only to increase motor speed

feedback.hint: Execution occurs with real sensors, loads, and disturbances, not an exact mathematical model.
feedback.solution: A plan is based on estimated state and a model. Feedback uses new measurements to correct disturbances and estimation or actuation errors.

questions.prompt: A planar two-link arm has link lengths 1.0 m and 0.5 m. The base frame x-axis is horizontal. Joint 1 is at 90° from the x-axis and joint 2 is at 0° relative to link 1. What is the y-coordinate of the end effector in the base frame? Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: Add the link contributions in the base frame, using the cumulative angle.
feedback.solution: The cumulative angle for both links is 90°, so both extend along +y: y = 1.0 sin 90° + 0.5 sin 90° = 1.5 m and x = 0. Tracking frame labels and cumulative angles prevents mixing joint-relative and base-frame angles.

questions.prompt: A two-link planar arm is fully extended (second joint at 0°). Which statement is correct?
options: Inverse kinematics always has one unique solution.
It has no singularity because the angles are zero.
Singularities only occur with three links.

It is at a kinematic singularity: the end effector cannot move radially inward or outward in the arm's reach direction for small joint motions, and elbow-up and elbow-down inverse solutions merge here but differ elsewhere.

feedback.hint: Think about the Jacobian when the links are collinear.
feedback.solution: At full extension the arm cannot extend further along its length, so the Jacobian loses rank; away from this pose there are two inverse solutions (elbow up and down), which coincide at the singularity.

questions.prompt: A motor delivers 0.10 N·m through a 20:1 gearbox with 80% efficiency. What is the output torque? Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: Multiply by the ratio and the efficiency.
feedback.solution: Output torque = 0.10 × 20 × 0.80 = 1.6 N·m. The output speed is divided by 20 (less friction losses); the convention for efficiency must be stated.

questions.prompt: Two independent position sensors each have a standard uncertainty of 3.0 mm. What is the standard uncertainty of their sum, in mm? Enter the value and unit.

feedback.hint: Independent uncertainties add in quadrature.
feedback.solution: √(3.0² + 3.0²) = 4.24 mm. A safety margin should be set from the combined uncertainty (for example a multiple of it), not from one sensor alone.

questions.prompt: A planar arm has L₁ = 0.3 m and L₂ = 0.2 m. With θ₁ = 30° and θ₂ = 45° (relative to link 1), what is the tool's x coordinate? Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: x = L₁ cos θ₁ + L₂ cos(θ₁ + θ₂).

questions.prompt: For the same arm and angles, what is the tool's y coordinate? Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: y = L₁ sin θ₁ + L₂ sin(θ₁ + θ₂).

questions.prompt: Find the elbow angle magnitude |θ₂| that places the tool of this arm (L₁ = 0.3, L₂ = 0.2 m) at (0.35, 0.15) m. Enter the number only, in degrees.

feedback.hint: cos θ₂ = (x² + y² − L₁² − L₂²)/(2L₁L₂).

questions.prompt: With θ₂ = +82.82°, find θ₁ for the target (0.35, 0.15) m. Enter the number only, in degrees.

feedback.hint: θ₁ = atan2(y, x) − atan2(L₂ sin θ₂, L₁ + L₂ cos θ₂).

questions.prompt: The tool is 0.4635 m from the base. Estimate the tool displacement caused by a 1° error at the base joint. Enter a value and unit.

feedback.hint: Arc length = radius × angle in radians.

questions.prompt: Which target can the arm (L₁ = 0.3 m, L₂ = 0.2 m) reach?
options: (0.30, 0.20) m, because its distance from the base (0.361 m) lies between 0.10 and 0.50 m.

feedback.hint: Reachable targets satisfy |L₁ − L₂| ≤ r ≤ L₁ + L₂.
feedback.solution: Distances: 0.361 m (reachable), 0.541 m (too far), 0.078 m (too close), 0.55 m (too far). Equivalently, cos θ₂ must lie in [−1, 1].

questions.prompt: The motor-side encoder resolves 0.037 mm at the tool, but the gearbox has 0.1° of backlash at the output (0.52 mm at the tool). Which statement is correct?

feedback.hint: What does the encoder measure, and where does the play occur?
feedback.solution: Play between gear teeth lets the output move without the motor shaft turning. Measuring after the gears, preloading, or approaching from one direction addresses it.

feedback.hint: Group by both task direction and elbow posture; report both velocity components.
feedback.solution: Each group has three deterministic reports. In02 has reduced inward speed about 2.09448 mm/s; other inward groups retain 10 mm/s and all tangential groups retain 10 mm/s.

questions.prompt: For q₁=0,q₂=2°,L₁=0.30 m,L₂=0.20 m and desired v=(−0.01,0) m/s, unconstrained q̇₂=0.01(L₁+L₂cosq₂)/(L₁L₂sinq₂). What q̇₂ in rad/s follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Convert the elbow angle to radians when evaluating the trigonometric terms.
feedback.solution: The requested elbow rate is approximately 2.387227 rad/s, exceeding the supplied 0.5 rad/s cap.

questions.prompt: At in02, unconstrained joint rates are approximately (−0.954542,2.387227) rad/s and both caps are 0.5 rad/s. What uniform scale min(1,0.5/max|q̇|) follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: The elbow rate has the largest magnitude and determines the common scale.
feedback.solution: The common scale is approximately 0.209448, preserving the frozen-Jacobian motion direction while reducing speed.

questions.prompt: At in02, the requested inward speed is 10 mm/s and common scale is approximately 0.209448. What achieved inward speed magnitude in mm/s follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Scale the desired task velocity by the same factor used for all joint rates.
feedback.solution: The achieved inward magnitude is approximately 2.094480 mm/s; it is a stipulated limiter effect, not measured hardware stalling.

questions.prompt: At exact straight horizontal extension, J=[0,0;0.5,0.2] and radial endpoint force F=(5,0) N. What first component of JᵀF in N·m follows? Enter the number only.

feedback.hint: Take the first column dot the stated force; do not invert J.
feedback.solution: The first torque contribution is zero, despite lost instantaneous radial motion. Internal structural load and dynamic motion are separate.

questions.prompt: Choose conclusions supported by this direction-dependent motion construction.

response_fields.prompt: What explains in02’s reduced mean inward speed?
options: The supplied uniform joint-speed limiter is active for its large inverse-rate demand.
A measured current limit proves a physical motor stalled.
A radial force always produces infinite joint torque.

response_fields.prompt: Why do the tangent groups retain 10 mm/s at every sampled posture?
options: Their inverse joint rates are ±1/30 rad/s and stay below the supplied caps.
Every task direction is equally conditioned near extension.
Tangential motion proves all hardware constraints are satisfied.

response_fields.prompt: What additional information does the preserved hardware-stall case need?
options: Synchronized joint/output motion, delivered actuation and calibrated load/frame information.
Only this toy CSV because it uniquely identifies the hardware fault.
Only endpoint reachability in an unconstrained simulation.

evidence: The dataset is constructed from a known rate limiter, without current or hardware observations.
The specific tangential request remains compatible with the supplied kinematic speed limits.
Geometry and the toy limiter do not identify a real stall cause.

feedback.hint: Keep known construction mechanisms separate from claims about a physical robot.
feedback.solution: The active common speed cap explains only the constructed inward slowdown; tangential feasibility and zero radial force moments do not establish actual hardware behavior.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the in90–in02 and ta90–ta02 near-extension reports follow from their declared construction? Select all that apply.
options: The in02 elbow command reaches the stipulated 0.5 rad/s cap.
The observed slowdown uniquely proves a physical gearbox fault.
Every singularity makes JᵀF diverge for every finite force.
Three report variants are deterministic and establish no real sensor-error distribution.
Uniform scaling preserves the desired direction under each frozen nonsingular Jacobian.

feedback.hint: Read the limiter, report-variation and force-map assumptions separately.
feedback.solution: The construction supports common scaling, an active elbow cap and deterministic variants. It contains no physical fault diagnosis or universal torque divergence.

questions.prompt: What can change if each unconstrained in02 joint rate is clipped independently to ±0.5 rad/s instead of scaled together?
options: The entire original desired velocity is always recovered.
The requested inward direction must be preserved because both commands are bounded.
The endpoint direction can change; with this J, the clipped rates (−0.5,+0.5) give approximately (0,−0.15) m/s.

feedback.hint: Multiply the clipped joint rates by the current Jacobian.
feedback.solution: Independent clipping gives zero x velocity and −0.15 m/s y velocity in this frozen model. A common scale instead retains the requested inward direction.
